image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a grey whale's back and dorsal area swimming in green water. The skin is dark grey with significant white mottling and barnacle clusters (callosities). A distinct longitudinal ridge runs along the spine. Part of a yellow object (likely a kayak or boat) is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up of the mid-back/dorsal region; the head and blowholes are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey coloration with white scarring and barnacle clusters typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no triangular dorsal fin. Instead, a series of low, rounded humps (knuckles) are visible trailing off towards the right side of the frame, consistent with Eschrichtius gibbosus anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The curvature of the back and the scale relative to the water surface suggest a massive, robust cylindrical body shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed across the entire visible surface; texture matches biological expectations for this species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Baleen plates are internal/oral structures not visible in an external dorsal shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally/laterally and are not visible in this top-down view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are outside the frame to the right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution details show rough, uneven skin texture with raised white areas indicative of callosities/barnacles.

To ensure the boundary between the whale and the water is sharp and physically consistent, checking for 'melting' edges common in AI generations.
To analyze the micro-texture of the barnacles and skin for signs of AI smearing or repetitive pattern artifacts.
To verify the displacement of water around the whale's body is physically accurate (wake and splash dynamics).
